SABRE Frontiersman 9.2 oz. Bear Spray, Maximum Strength 2.0% Major Capsaicinoids, Powerful 35 ft. Range Bear Deterrent, Outdoor Camping & Hiking Protection, Quick Draw Holster & Multipack Options Just like verifying that you are comfortable using a pistol or rifle, you also have to know that any weapon that you have reason to depend on is functional and loaded. It's only common sense to test out any weapon prior to depending on it to defend yourself and/or your family. A firearm that goes "click" when you pull the trigger is of no use to you -- and neither is this Sabre Bear Spray if the can/fixture is faulty or filled with ineffective spray.

When I was in the pepper spray distribution business many years ago, I always had to test out sample batches of the product to make sure that the sprayer worked and the spray itself was as powerful as promised. I got tired of being sprayed in the face (like all police officers who carry a personal defense spray are required to do) so I devised an alternative test that was not as intrusive or disabling.

Taking the canister outside of our building, I'd find a quiet space with no wind and spray a small amount on the back of my hand. That accomplishes two things; it shows that the can is pressurized and discharges properly and it also demonstrates how irritating the spray is to the back of your hand. As you will find out for yourself, a good can will provide an instant burning sensation. However you must be extremely careful to not get it in your eyes or transfer it to other parts of your exposed skin. That can end up being almost as bad as taking a full blast in the face.

My youngest daughter and my wife each carries one of these units. SABRE has always been highly regarded in the industry but in the past I did test one of their products and find it to be totally ineffective. They took care of the problem, replaced the faulty unit with a good one, and now I feel that my wife and daughter have the advantage in a confrontation should they practice "situational awareness" and keep their wits about them. I told them to keep spraying until the criminal, dog, or whatever threat targeting them is down for the count and does not remain a danger to them. They each have a concealed carry permit so I am confident that if they have to they can move on to the next step.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Frontiersman 9.2 oz. Bear Spray, Maximum Strength 2.0% Major Capsaicinoids, Powerful 35 ft. Range Bear Deterrent, Outdoor Camping & Hiking Protection, Quick Draw Holster & Multipack Options

Ringside 100-pound Powerhide Boxing Punching Heavy Bag (Soft Filled) Black, 100 LBS My wife and I got into using a heavy bag about six months prior to Covid, when we were taking Kickboxing training at a local facility. We loved it. During Covid, we decided to get a home set (Everlast stand and heavy bag) so we could keep going while locked down and onward. We loved that set, but found the bag (75 lbs) to be too light for us, and decided to get a heavier for a Christmas gift to ourselves. We went with a 100 lbs, bag.

We have used Ringside at the training studio and have their gloves, so we knew the product line, and decided to take a look at a home bag. Originally we were going to go for a longer bag for kicking, but settled on this Ringside 100-pound Powerhide Boxing Punching Heavy Bag to fit our current set up - not ideal for kicking. As renters we can only do so much, so being able to move and adjust, keeping things a bit more mobile, was the key. We bought this Ringside 100-pound Powerhide Boxing Punching Heavy Bag with the intention of being able to use it for boxing now, being able to move it when we move, and that it can work with our Everlast frame. The frame takes up to 100 lbs.

So far we are very happy with the Ringside 100-pound Powerhide Boxing Punching Heavy Bag as our choice. I cannot imagine not having another Ringside - we have come to like the product line very much. The materials are excellent and withstand our skills. But they also give us something reliable and long lasting. The stitching for the attaching rings is excellent as well - it should withstand everything we can throw at it. The top ring allows for the bag to turn - which is great and not making out stand need to be readjusted as we sometimes had to do with the Everlast bag that does not have a similar turning mechanism. There is a ring at the bottom as well, so we can anchor it if we decide - to keep it from swaying as much. We are currently choosing not to use that ring. In the end, we are once again truly impressed with and happy to have made the choice of a Ringside. Everything we have experienced to date has been top notch. It’s only been a few weeks, but from previous experience, we believe it’ll last - our future plans include being able to mount to a ceiling, but for now, the stand mount is perfect. It all adds up to giving us what we need to workout.
text_fidelity_b: Ringside 100-pound Powerhide Boxing Punching Heavy Bag (Soft Filled) Black, 100 LBS

Kettler Travel Tour Set Pannier Set Two very handsome collapsible grocery-bag panniers, highly water resistant if not classified as waterproof, & an "overnighter" sized suitcase.
I cannot verify the stated 57 liter capacity of this set-up. I can testify that my measurements came to 51.5 liters, thereabouts. A standard large grocery bag is 6.5 inches by 11.5 inches...then there's the length...these panniers are 11/11.5 inches high. Doing the math comes to 1719 cubic inches for the pair...more of less.
The suitcase measures 19 by 12.5 by 6. so that's 1425 cu. in. Add it to the panniers comes to 3144 cu. in. or 51.5 liters.
Aside from this little discrepancy about capacity this is a well made good looking carrier system. You can toss the suitcase in the closet and still have a competent set of pannier bags that will attach to any rack. And you can still plunk your rack-bag of choice on top. I think they were called trunk bags also. Kettler took the terminology out to the proper dimensions by designing the suitcase. Velcro plus buckles hold it on top.
The panniers come collapsed inside the suitcase. All you need do is slide the ends of the plastic stays away from the thread band...you don't need to cut the thread...you can leave it in place, and then tuck the plastic ends all around the inside the pannier. And wah lah a firm & rigid pannier body all around. I did say good looking? How waterproof I don't know. No instructions. We're on our own.
I wanted a set-up like this some time ago. My delema is getting six loaves of bread home. Light but lots of volume. This system seemed the way to go. But the original price stunk. Once again Amazon to the rescue. Thanks one more time Amazon. And thanks as well for the price for the "trunk" bag from Topeak as well!
text_fidelity_b: Kettler Travel Tour Set Pannier Set

text_fidelity_a:
UVPaqlite Tooblite I recently bought several UVPaqlite items, and have had some time to test them out. Out of the 4 items I purchased, this was reasonably impressive. With fair exposure to light, it will glow strong for 10 minutes. Around the 15 minute mark, it has faded a bit, but is still bright enough that you can still read with it in total darkness, with adjusted eyes. By 60 minutes, it's faintly visible in a dark room, with your eyes adjusted. Even by 90 minutes, it's still faintly visible, but only just barely.

Out of the 4 UVPaqlite items I purchased, this didn't glow as strong or last as long as the UVPaqlite packets - however, that seemed natural, given its tubular design (less surface area exposed to the viewer). The clear resin had a lot of bubbles, which seemed to diffuse the glow a bit - making for a more even light, but also limiting its range. However, the tubular design is also its biggest strength. Compared to the UVPaqlite packets - which are fairly rugged in their own right - this seems much more durable, as well as convenient to carry or mount. As such, I mounted this next to my quick-release home shotgun mount. In the event the lights immediately go out, I can quickly - even before my eyes have adjusted - find my flashlight and unlock the shotgun, should I need it.

If you need stronger and longer lasting light, I recommend the UVPaqlite vacuum-sealed packets. Both the [[ASIN:B00698NBYE UVPaqlite Medium]] and [[ASIN:B00698HB1I UVPaqlite Mini]] out-performed the Tooblites I bought, as far as effective brightness. However, consider that the Tooblite shape is more convenient for certain tasks. As well, while these "charge and glow" phosphorescent products have their purposes, they can't replace a flashlight or chemiluminescence glow stick when you need on-demand light. So, consider what you might use them for, before purchasing.
text_fidelity_b: UVPaqlite Tooblite

Ankle straps. Wow! They're comfortable. I really want expecting much for this price range, and the ankle straps are definitely worth it. Time will tell how durable they are, but I think I'll get my money's worth out of them.

Wrist wraps. Again, I wasn't expecting much. Never used wrist straps before, but I did choose this bundle because, hey what the heck, they're included. I don't have experience using the wrist straps, so I have no idea how they compare to others. They do provide support to my wrists. The thumb loop should have been sewn in so that it wraps nicely around your thumb though. Instead there's the one side that had to fold over because it was sewn as a flat loop. I'll give them a try.

Resistance loops. They're thin. I guess I was expecting them to be a little thicker. They do give resistance and I'm sure I'll find ways to use them. The heavier ones do make me sore on the outsides of my thighs, so they are doing what they're intended for, adding resistance.

Resistance bands. They're thin. They do seem to have the appropriate ratings though compared to other more expensive resistance bands that I have. I was looking for bands with these kind of attachment points. They're more versatile than the ones that have to hook into their own proprietary handles and attachments.

I do wish that they sold sets of just the bands though. Because there's not enough of the higher weight bands in this set for all of my needs. I'll end up buying other set just for extra bands.

The towel. A decent towel for working out. Again, I've never used one in the gym. But I'll find a use for it.

Door anchor. This thing is not going to slip through the door unintentionally. Just remember to put it through the hinge side of the door. Doors don't have enough strength on the latch side or top.

Sliders. They're about the same size and basic construction as another set of sliders that I have. But the ones in this set seem to be tacky on the smooth side. So if you're using them on carpet, you'll need to wear shoes or socks with some grip. Otherwise, you're foot will slide off and the slider will stay put.

I buy a product for being in an acceptable price to quality ratio that works for me. If I like it, I buy again. I don't care who is making it or selling it.

text_fidelity_a:
5.11 Tactical Bail Out Bag Molle Ammo Magazine Carrier Pack for Responders , Style 56026 5.11 is a well-known and highly regarded supplier of tactical equipment. This is a well-constructed bag made of a double-stitched tough nylon material that uses heavy duty zippers and large Velcro fasteners to keep everything locked down. It will hold six 30 rd mags of .223 ammo (or several other ammo combinations) securely and within easy reach. I put a piece of old towel between each pair of mags to help minimize any noises while moving around.

Behind the mag pockets is a deep compartment that can hold an effective combination of equipment. If you're like me, you'll want to also isolate any equipment in that main compartment to avoid shifting and noise generation. Each side of the bag has an additional zippered compartment that can hold pistol mags, a flashlight or other tools. The padded and adjustable shoulder strap can be configured to hang around your neck and allow the bag to be centered on your lower belly and there is a Velcro belt loop on the inside of the bag so that you can anchor it to a 2" belt. I prefer to have the bag centered so that I can get to what I need quickly with either hand.

This 5.11 Tactical Bail Out Bag is a well-made and practically designed grab bag that can be filled with critical supplies should you need to get out of your home in a hurry. The main problem I see is that the very bottom of the main compartment seems to be constructed of a thinner material. Unfortunately, because this large main compartment will hold a lot of stuff, the combined weight and/or sharp edges of whatever is being carried is likely to wear through that area first. This area needs to be reinforced by sewing in extra fabric or by the insertion of a fitted piece of foam. Either quick fix should add extra durability to this weak point. I'm very surprised that 5.11 didn't pay more attention to this part of the bag. Perhaps in the near future their bags will come out with some type of reinforced bottom.
text_fidelity_b: 5.11 Tactical Bail Out Bag Molle Ammo Magazine Carrier Pack for Responders , Style 56026

text_fidelity_a:
SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Presta Valve Tubes, Multiple Sizes I ordered two Sunlite (Kenda) Thorn resistant tubes (700c x 18/23) with removable presta core in July of 2015. I wanted a thick (puncture resistant) tube that allowed me to remove the core (with a chain tool) to allow me to inject tire sealant into the tube.

In the Southwest, we have nasty thorns called 'goatheads' that cause many flats. As part of my defense system, I use: 1) a thick, thorn resistant tube, 2) tire sealant (Flat Attack); 3) a high-quality, super puncture-resistant tire (Schwalbe - Marathon Plus Tour, Marathon Supreme, or Durano Plus - depending on the bike).

I waited a while to see how these Sunlite tubes would hold up. Unfortunately, after about a year and a half, the front tube failed. The presta valve stem separated from the tube, rendering the tube unrepairable and useless. The rear tube got a flat, but due to the tire sealant, I was able to simply pump up the tire, spin the wheel, and it sealed itself.

I had high hopes for these tubes, but I will look for other alternatives.

TIP: One reason that many of these tubes may be failing at the stem is due to the threaded, round 'nut' on the valve stem. The nut is really helpful when inflating the tube for the FIRST time, (i.e., when there is no air in it). However, once inflated to full pressure, I would recommend REMOVING this nut and setting it aside. The problem is that when riding with this nut tightened down on the valve stem, it creates added pressure on the stem at the base of the tube, increasing the likelihood of separation & failure.
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Presta Valve Tubes, Multiple Sizes

I was a bit disappointed that the company no longer offered the original Fitbit One, so bought this to replace it. I actually love it, except for the clunkiness of the look. I also like having the reminder that encourages me to get at least 250 steps an hour. I find that quite motivating, and enjoy the tiny, animated celebration when I meet my goal. text_fidelity_a: NordicTrack T Series Treadmills There is one huge flaw in this machine...and that is if you intend to use the incline feature you will no longer be able to reach anything out in front of you, meaning you can not reach your water bottle...music device...digital read out display...or even to use the heart rate grip handles.  If you look at the machine in the pictures...you will notice a black plastic insert that runs on top of the actual tread mill just below the display.  As you incline the machine...this part of the treadmill comes closer to you....meaning you have to move more backwards on the machine in order to avoid stepping on it.  You have to move back so far that you literally have to bend over at the waist just to use the heart rate grips.  I found myself keep having to step on the sides off the treadmill and stop my walk anytime I wanted to change my music or change a feature on the unit.  Very very frustrating. If you walk for say 30 to 60 minutes and you watch videos on youtube or something like that...you will have to literally stop walking and step off the machine as many times as the videos run out...or your music choice changes.  I don't hold onto the rail in front of me anyway, but if you are someone who does...you will not be able to do so with the unit inclined.  You will keep stepping on the plastic piece and can literally injure yourself the first time you do it.  Machine seems nice otherwise but this is to huge of a flaw to give it anything but 1 star.  I guess everyone else is not using the incline feature.  And no...I am not 8 feet tall....with long legs. Only 5'10" and my wife is 5'1" and has the same issue.  Just note the above and take into consideration when purchasing. I wouldn't buy this unit again...and already put together and box tore up to return.  Frustrating.
text_fidelity_b: NordicTrack T Series Treadmills

text_fidelity_a:
Source Tactical Assault 20L Hydration Backpack - Includes 3L WLPS Low Profile Hydration Bladder - High-Flow Storm Drinking Valve - MOLLE Webbing for Equipment Attachment, Coyote This is a comfortable back pack.
The selling point for me was that it was listed to be able to accept an additional water bladder. And for me, (I hike in the Phoenix, AZ area mountains during the midday summer heat) that is important. Two 3liter bladders are a standard for me. Normally, I have to move up to my 35 litter backpack during the summer because the straps on my other packs are too narrow to adequately support the weight of two 3liter bladders (6 kilos or about 13lbs) in addition to my emergency first aid supplies, food, phone, and anything else I have. In total, about 25lbs (a little more than 11 kilos).

So it was a pleasant surprise that the straps on this 20 liter pack were almost as wide as the straps on my 35 liter pack. Making this pack easily able to comfortably carry the weight.

Also the waist belt has molle webbing for attaching additional things. For me, that's a phone carrier on one side and a 4x6 pouch on the other for some trail snacks (if I need the nourishment on the trail). A big plus. I don't have to remove the backpack to have a snack or to put the empty wrapper back in the pouch.
The waist belt also helps keep everything stable when I am trail running (probably about half of my normal 10 mile hike is trail running)

The padding on this backpack is much better than any of my other backpacks regardless of size. (I have 3l,6l,12l,18l,20l,25l,30l, and 35l backpacks.) Yes, I have a lot because I've never been able to find a nearly perfect fit for my needs, until now.

The bladder - this is a high quality bladder. (I now have four of them.) It has a nice high water flow. I'm easily drinking more during my hike because of this high flow rate. With my other bladders, I averaged about 1 liter an hour consumption. With these bladders, I average 1.5 liters an hour consumption. I have my garmin watch set to give a reminder every 8 minutes to drink water. So with the old bladders and the new Source bladders, I was drinking at the same intervals, it's just easier to drink through the Source drinking tube than the other ones resulting in the higher consumption.

Strap management - this thing has elastic on each of the straps to hold the excess strapping. Wow, so nice. No Irish pennants (marine corps terminology referring to the the stray threads sticking out on clothing) flying all over the place

I do have one complaint though, it says that it'll accept a second bladder. But there's only the one strap in the water bladder compartment to hold a bladder. To accommodate a second bladder, you have to place it in the main storage compartment. But there is no strap to hold a bladder there. And you have farther to run the tube for this second bladder. I started keeping some storage at the bottom of the main compartment (sun block, towels, etc.) that manages to raise up the second bladder so that the drinking tube for that bladder isn't uncomfortably short to drink through. Otherwise the second bladder sits low enough that the tube is a little short (perhaps about 5 or 6 inches shorter than the tube for the water bladder in the water bladder compartment).
text_fidelity_b: Source Tactical Assault 20L Hydration Backpack - Includes 3L WLPS Low Profile Hydration Bladder - High-Flow Storm Drinking Valve - MOLLE Webbing for Equipment Attachment, Coyote

text_fidelity_a: Grabber Outdoors Stainless Steel Adjustable Pocket Stove With 8 Fuel Tabs For many years, I've used Esbit / hexamine fuel tabs with a similar folding stove.  It's not my primary heat source, but rather I use it for times I need a little quick fire, or to get larger fires started.  One tab is enough to get 2 cups of water boiling, in most weather conditions.  The stove works fairly well with most mess kit items.  But, I more regularly use parts of a tab as tinder to get larger sticks going, so I build a bigger fire.  I can cook larger things on the large fire, and then I'll move some coals to the folding stove to heat up smaller items, or put hot rocks into it for portable heat.  The stove isn't all that rugged, but it holds up better than my improvised soda can stoves, and packs up very nicely (you can fit 4 tabs in the stove when it's folded).  I've also used trioxane, but the Esbit / hexamine tabs burn cleaner and hotter for longer, and are easier to find deals on.  For casual trips, where I don't need a big fire, don't carry any kind of gas fuel, sticks may not be plentiful, or I just need to heat up some coffee or a freeze dried meal - the combination of this stove, one hexamine tab and a steel cup works perfectly for me.  At such a low price, I won't feel guilty using up the tabs, or if the stove gets a little beat up.
text_fidelity_b: Grabber Outdoors Stainless Steel Adjustable Pocket Stove With 8 Fuel Tabs

Lanzom® Outdoor Camouflage Bucket Hats Mesh Sun Hat Boonie Fishing Hats The orange hat I ordered was SO UGLY that I actually had to order a different color (the navy) for myself at full price so I could write a fair review. I was fortunate to be able to purchase the orange one at a discount and I was hoping to receive the bright, punchy tangerine color shown in the example image. Instead I received a burnt orange hat with a bright orange mesh band and all of it is HIDEOUS. I was so upset that I had "wasted" my discount! Luckily my 9 year old is willing to wear the hat which is good because I can't return it. I can promise you this orange hat will never be stolen. EVER.

The pictures I included were taken in natural daylight and they don't accurately capture just how ugly and mis-matched the orange hat is. The body of the hat is a burnt blood orange color. It is remarkably ugly, even for University of Texas fans. The mesh band is safety orange - very similar to the neon orange color deer hunters sometimes wear. In person, the colors clash so badly that it really is only appropriate for a 9 year old boy to wear because it is assumed he doesn't know any better. And even then it is only suitable to wear fishing. Alone, so no one sees the hat. On a windy lake where you have the best chance of losing it.

The Navy hat is a million times better. It, too, does not match its example image but in a good way. The hat is a deep, dark midnight navy shade with a dark navy band that matches the hat body. It looks very nice. If I could do it over again I would select the black or navy for myself. Anything but this orange hat!

The hat itself is very comfortable and lightweight. I love the feel of it, how breathable it is and that the strap is very loose and lightweight. (I can't stand the feeling of things around my chin and neck or the sensation that cords are choking me.) This hat is pleasantly comfortable, bounces back from being crushed (or thrown across the room and trampled underfoot until the navy hat arrived because it was so danged ugly) and it seems like it will shed water well if splashed.

I was fortunate to be able to purchase this hat at a discount, I just picked the wrong color. I liked the hat well enough to buy it at full price in another color that I am actually willing to wear. I REALLY wished I had bought any color but the orange! I hope that by sharing my experience and photos that you are able to make the best buying decision! (Hint: ORANGE is the wrong answer!)

Klymit Maxfield Backpacking Tent, Lightweight 2-Person Tent for Camping and Hiking Honestly this tent is great, especially at the sale price it periodically goes down to. It is literally lighter than my previous 1-person tent. The stakes it comes with are great which is rare, plenty of guy-lines already attached and coiled up at the tie-off points, no issues with ventilation or heat retention in the 3-seasons it is designed for. The rainfly, footprint, and base of the tent all clip together quite nicely and have adjustment sliders to keep them correctly tensioned. The single piece pole assembly is a little counter-intuitive, but it works great once you orient it.

HOWEVER: get the footprint for it.

I bring a scrap of tarp to throw under the footprints of all my tents anyways, because a sharp, half buried rock can always ruin things, but you don't need to. A significant amount of the versatility and convenience goes away without the footprint that is designed for it, like the ability to throw the footprint and rainfly together as an emergency shelter in a few moments, or use it in an ultralight configuration to save even more weight.
The only potential concern i have is that with how light this material is, I don't know what long term durability will be. It is VERY light material, and that usually trades out durability. Time will tell.
text_fidelity_b: Klymit Maxfield Backpacking Tent, Lightweight 2-Person Tent for Camping and Hiking

text_fidelity_a:
Soddeph 1.3 Gallon Collapsible Water Container Bag, BPA Free Food Grade Clear Plastic Storage Jug for Sport Camping Riding Mountaineer,Freezable,Food Grade (1.3 Gal, 2-pack) As we live in a hurricane prone area we decided to add these to our preparedness collection. Along with our gallons of water we thought it would be a good idea to grab these. Unlike the gallon we’ll full these bags up last minute and use for cooking and cleaning water. They are very large and store a good amount of water, and with the their base that speaks out and sits well, it’ll be good to have around. But they don’t seem like they’ll be able to sit and hold water as we do for the entire 6 month season with our normal gallon jugs. No problem, again, we’ll fill them as a storm is approaching and use for short term storage.

The materials (plastic) seem like they’ll hold up. We have found with the gallon jugs there are quality differences: some are thin and will start to leak after a few months. We also do not keep them from season to season. As a season hits it’s end we’ll use that water for water and cooking and then restock for the next season. With these jugs we’ll fill as the storm approaches, then empty after it’s through and water is no longer needed.

I THINK I’ll be able to fill in the sink, but have not tried. It is large and we’d prefer doing a good cleaning on the sink before laying it inside. I did not take that time and instead filled it from the tub. That worked okay. I lost a good amount of water as the flow from that spigot is not great. But it filled in a few minutes and will sit fine.

Overall it’ll be a good back up and we’re happy to have them for our set up. Should we ever go camping (not something we do) or need water in a pinch, we’ll find other uses. But just the prep element is well worth having these around.
text_fidelity_b: Soddeph 1.3 Gallon Collapsible Water Container Bag, BPA Free Food Grade Clear Plastic Storage Jug for Sport Camping Riding Mountaineer,Freezable,Food Grade (1.3 Gal, 2-pack)

Eackrola 2/4-Person-Tent, Instant Pop up Tent for Camping, Easy Setup Beach Tent Sun Shelter - Ventilated Mesh Windows, Water Resistant, Carry Bag Included I got this tent to have a little pop up tent for the beach. I was assuming it was pretty small, easy to pack in the car and to the beach. But this tent is quite large. In its case it comes up to my waist or so (Iʻm 5ʻ7"). When opened up it easily fits my entire family inside. So itʻs a little large for my intended use, but I think it will be very useful when family camping.

Setting up this tent is the very definition of simple. I took it out of itʻs case and threw it on the ground. At first it took a while to open up, since all the windows and doors were shut and creating a vacuum in the tent. But once I cracked a window and air could get in it popped right open. The tent is quite spacious. I can lie down the short way and not touch the walls of the tent. If you are very tall, you probably would have to lie down the long way in the tent though. I canʻt stand up in the tent, itʻs about the height of your standard 4 man dome tent.

There are doors on either end, both with screens and rain flies. There are also windows on both sides. The windows have a zipper, so you can pass small objects through the window.

Breaking down this tent was challenging. It took me quite a while to figure it out. I watched the promotional video for this tent which briefly showed how to put away the tent. It was slightly helpful, but I was still confused. But now that I figured out how to do it, I can get it broken down pretty quickly, within 20-30 seconds at the most.

I think this tent will be great for a quick camping trip with the family when I donʻt want to lug around our huge cabin tent. Putting it up is simple, there is more than enough space for me, my wife, and two kids, and it is now pretty quick to break down. Even if we do bring the big tent, I think we will still use this tent. Either the kids can have their own tent or have it as a play area.

DoublePlus Fan for The OG Bike, Strong Clip Fan for The OG Bike & Bike+, USB Chargable Fan for The Bike, Portable Fan Adjustable 3 Speed, Accessories Compatible with The Bike As I sit here and write this review for the DoublePlus Fan for Peloton I have had the fan blowing on me for the past two hours as I've worked. It's been great!

My little corner of the house where my office is can get pretty warm, but our workout bike is over here and... I turned it on and have been comfortable ever since! So first, we actually have another brand of indoor bike, but this DoublePlus Fan for Peloton works perfectly on the handle where it's currently mounted. We've both been sick a few weeks and haven't been on the bike, but when we get back to it, we'll have to figure out a bit better place to mount it - but on the handle bar it works fine, opens well enough, and stays securely. It has a goose neck arm to is, so I was able to raise it high and turn it and it's been on me - as mentioned above - without a single issue. And as mentioned, it's been at least two hours. It arrived already charged, and continues to go strong - on the lowest level. The sound is not disturbing my work nor the shows I've been streaming online as I've worked today.

The DoublePlus Fan for Peloton arrived in a nice, plain black box, perfect for gifting if you choose. It would also make a good place to store the instructions, cord, and/or fan if you wanted to. We'll hold onto it for just such a plan. The lit button is the on/off and works easily - click as you peddle or walk by - as I do. The clamp is wide enough to go on our handle bars, but could also mount on something like a desk or shelf, the grip strips holding it in place and enough variance of width for a few different sizes. I'd be careful not to overdo, but it should hold up to decent pressure. We have not - yet - had to charge, but it should be easy, based on what we're seeing. I'll update if anything changes in the coming months, but as of this writing, I'm comfortable, and this little DoublePlus Fan for Peloton has been a great find!

text_fidelity_a: Milepetus 350/700Pcs Fishing Bobber Stopper,7 in 1 Soft Silicone Transparent Float Sinker Stops,Rubber Oval Cylinder Float Stop Stoppers (Transparent- Cylinder, S (700pcs)) I use these, not as slip cork stops, but as a method of affixing a hopper dropper. I run my leader through the eye of the hopper. Do not tie to the eye. Feed the stopper onto the barb with the wire facing forward toward the eye of the hook. Pull about a foot of leader through the wire loop then pull the loop back through the stop which will pull the leader through the stop. I then tie on my dropper. This allows you to set the depth of the dropper simply by pulling the dropper up or down. Note that I use the small. The amount of tension on the line is controlled by the tippet size as well as the hook size of the hopper. The larger the diameter of the hook the smaller the tippet size that can be used. You just have to experiment for your needs. I find a size 8 hook and #5 tippet hold well. This is one of the best methods I have found for an adjustable  strike indicator.
text_fidelity_b: Milepetus 350/700Pcs Fishing Bobber Stopper,7 in 1 Soft Silicone Transparent Float Sinker Stops,Rubber Oval Cylinder Float Stop Stoppers (Transparent- Cylinder, S (700pcs))

text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer This is the 2nd pedometer I've owned. I bought this Omron to replace Walk 4 Life (W4L) unit I used for the prior 7 months. I was happy with the W4L pedometer except that the clip broke twice on it. And, because the clip is part of the basic W4L housing, you can't just purchase another clip - the unit is basically ruined (unless you want to risk carrying it loose in your pocket and opening it with your thumbnail). Therefore, since this Omron pedometer fits inside a separate hard plastic clip housing, I decided to try it.

It functions well, accurately tracks your steps, and has a nice memory feature to review the past week. However, it is close to 3 times the size of the W4L and, therefore, too bulky to wear under nice clothes. I was able to clip the W4L to my bra under a relatively tight fitting top, and it was undetectable; the Omron looks like a growth is projecting out of your chest. This seems to defeat the purpose of tracking all your steps if you can't (or choose not to) wear it, let's say, on a night you go dancing. In addition, although there's much less chance of the clip breaking, it's uncomfortable against bare skin and seems to me to be much bulkier than necessary.

In spite of these design flaws, it's a nice little unit for wearing around the house or in a casual/workout environment. In general, I've found pedometers to be a fantastic way to motivate individuals to just stay active, which is much more effective than exercise alone. If the only way pedometer manufacturers can prevent the clips from breaking is to make them as Omron has, it's far better than W4L's clip design.

If Omron could reduce the size of the unit, the bulkiness of the clip, and have the unit sit low in the clip housing (instead of half of it sticking up over the top), I'd give it 5 stars.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-112 Digital Pocket Pedometer

text_fidelity_a: Brooks England Cambium All Weather Bike Seat - High Mileage, Waterproof, Carved/Standard Bicycle Saddle (C15, C17, C19) I have to say I was really disappointed by this saddle.  I have never ridden a brooks saddle or leather saddle before but I would not rate this as comfortable. The cutout and overall size of the seat felt right, I just couldn't get past the very firm feel of the material.  Immediately after sitting on it I could feel my sit bones making direct contact with the material and the material not offering any sense of relief.  I did give this saddle about 40 miles before deciding it was not for me. I will admit the seat seemed to maintain the same level of comfort for the entire trip which is an improvement over other saddles I've owned, which become unbearable after 20 miles.  This saddle never felt unbearable no matter the time spent on it.  I am a large guy, weighing in at 220 lbs, which is what I am attributing to my issue. I did replace it with a gel saddle and it initially feels much better.  I have a feeling if you carry less weight, the lack of padding might work for you.
text_fidelity_b: Brooks England Cambium All Weather Bike Seat - High Mileage, Waterproof, Carved/Standard Bicycle Saddle (C15, C17, C19)

text_fidelity_a: HCI Fitness PhysioTrainer Upper Body Ergonometer Recovering from triple-bypass open heart surgery, I got to use a high-end version of  this ergonometer at rehab. Since heart-surgery patients aren't supposed to lift anything heavy for a while, my arms were just hanging there for months, muscle-atrophy setting in. This exercise is a great way to bring the arms 'back to life' without any heavy lifting. The hospital rehab version no doubt costs a few thousand dollars, the HCI Fitness model cost under $500. Yet it seems comparable and does the job. I do at least 15 to 20 minutes a day on this while watching television. The TV is a nice distraction so you don't focus on the built-in timer, it's actually pleasant to use and will make your arms toned, whether you're a recovering heart patient, or are just looking for a good way to move those arms and get the benefits. The adjustable resistance is a plus and the unit is completely silent in operation. I have had this only three months but see no reason it won't serve me for years to come. By the way, the pedals have straps to also exercise the legs, but I use this only for my arms, I have an exercise bike for the legs.
text_fidelity_b: HCI Fitness PhysioTrainer Upper Body Ergonometer

text_fidelity_a:
Eafengrow EF953 Pocket Folding Knife G10 Handle D2 Blade,EDC Tool Knife for Outdoor Camping Hiking (Black) NGL, it's a slick looking knife, but it isn't well constructed.

The blade looks good and the scales feel good in the hand. The blade definitely is sharp. The issue is the pivot point of the knife and the scales around the pivot point.

You'll notice that there is a nice index finger groove up near the pivot point. This is a nice ergo component, however when gripping the knife here the scales flex and cause a severe amount of blade play at the pivot point. Inversely, grabbing the blade towards the base and wigging it will cause the scales at that finger well to flex.

As much as I would like to write this off as a 1-off construction issue, I had an unrelated individual talk about the very same issue they had with this knife. They had sourced the knife from their local B&M and had mentioned the issue. I told them I had one in the mail and would check it when the knife showed up. Sure enough 2 instances of this knife with the same issue.

So buyer beware. I have heard good things about this knife maker and this knife so I decided to test the waters with this blade. I will be sending this knife back and I doubt I will be buying another Eafengrow even if it's another G-10 D2 for sub $20.
text_fidelity_b: Eafengrow EF953 Pocket Folding Knife G10 Handle D2 Blade,EDC Tool Knife for Outdoor Camping Hiking (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
IRON COMPANY Body-Solid Leverage Squat/Calf Machine Let me start by saying I have been lifting in gyms for about 30 years and even qualified for Nationals as bodybuilder when I was 27....I'm 43 now. Still going at it strong but wanted a home calf raise machine and an alternative to barbell squats. I've probably lifted on just about any and all commercial grade equipment out there. Here are my thoughts on this piece of equipment and why I only gave it 3 stars. I hope it helps.

1) As others have stated...there are no directions and let's be serious...how irritating is that? If you can't bother giving your customer assembly instructions how much can you really honestly care about your customer? Just my two cents.

2) The contents are ill packaged and yes, I understand that Fed Ex shakes the boxes. But both boxes looked like they were packaged by a 5 year old. Just a total mess...screws...bolts...washer...thrown around in the box with shredded styrofoam and broken tight downs. I can't possibly see how any shipper could have created this total mess. Again, extreme sloppiness leads me to believe there is a lack of concern for the person receiving it.

3) 50% of the reason I purchased this piece of equipment was for the standing calf raise, my local gym only has the seated calf raise. I've had this exact same piece of equipment before by PowerTec....and I wasn't sure how I was going to feel about the rounded calf raise platform versus the flat one that power tec made and every other commercial grade piece of gym equipment uses. Now I know why they don't use a rounded platform. U have less contact material with your foot when you raise up. Is it the end of the world? No...but I'm just not a huge fan of the rounded platform. I much more prefer the standard flat platform that feels natural and more comfortable on the feet.

4) The step up from floor level to the calf raise machine is a bit hairy once you get some heavy weight on the machine...3 to 4...45's on each side. I wish the platform was designed differently so all that weight is not stacked onto on leg and your back is torqued when you step up. Commercial grade equipment is made in such a way that the platform is directly under you....you start on the calf platform...you don't load the weight and then step up. This machine is set up so that in order to have the weight directly on your shoulders...where it needs to be....you are standing one step behind the calf platform. Then in order to do the calf raise...you have to step up onto the platform...one leg at at time with all the weight on your back and one leg down...and one leg taking a step. Not good in my opinion.

5) The angle of the squat. Ahh...its okay....makes you feel like you are doing a deep squat but in reality even a deep squat on this machine is not even a parallel squat. If you have someone else do a deep squat and watch their lower leg in relation to their upper...you will see that the deepest squat on this machine is still a high squat in reality. Your leg is simply at a different angle and gives the false sense that you are performing a deep squat...when in fact you are not.

Will this take the place of a regular squat?

Yes, and No.

If you are a gym rat and you perform squats correctly than this piece of equipment will never take the place of or produce the same results.

If you are like 95% of the guys in the gym that never ever reach parallel when they squat because they were too busy stacking on the weight instead of learning good form at the beginning...than yes...this piece of equipment will keep you squatting a bit high and allow you to keep stacking the weight on and the ego flying high.

Can you get a good calf workout on this machine?

Absolutely. Even with the rounded platform that I do not like...you can still get a great calf workout.

Would I buy it again?

I'm on the fence with this one. I wouldn't cry if it was removed from my home...but I wouldn't send it back either.

I use the squat portion in addition to my leg workout....not as my primary piece of equipment...and I think that is what it is good for...and addition to regular squats....leg press...lungs...extensions...curls...etc. etc.

Hope my review helped somone.
text_fidelity_b: IRON COMPANY Body-Solid Leverage Squat/Calf Machine

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness Incline Full Motion Rowing Machine Rower with 350 lb Weight Capacity and LCD Monitor I purchased this unit, and it unfortunately arrived at my condo while I was out of town and my return window expired, or I would have returned it. I’m 63 years old, over 6 feet tall, and a large man. I go about 350 and ordered this unit because it will handle my weight, and it is built quite strong. I’m not sure where they got the child in the picture, but the unit just isn’t as big as it looks in the picture. The unit is built fairly strong, but is too low to the ground and too narrow at the base to be safe for large people. And there is no way to really adjust the pull force requirement, which is a lot if you are heavy.
If you are a large person and want to really use this machine, get a piece of plywood that’s at least 8 inches wider and longer than the base, mount 2 4x4s (stacked) to the front, and one 4x4 on the rear. Then mount the unit to the 4x4s and prepare for a real upper body workout. (Raising the front will allow you to get on the thing without the seat sliding downhill while you get on it). Overall, if you are a 20 year old 100 pounder, this is probably a good unit for you. If you are large, or over 30, you should look elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Incline Full Motion Rowing Machine Rower with 350 lb Weight Capacity and LCD Monitor
